transitions.summary: Wording only, on period rulings (round 037, 2026-09-29). The record claimed: The era card has no once-per-turn limit, so a copy banished again during the same End Phase (for example by Bottomless Trap Hole) returns again; the modern card returns once per turn. The modern card checks that it is currently banished and was banished this turn; the era trigger is claimed to have no still-banished check. A period ruling in force says otherwise: Konami TCG Card FAQ default_de page (Internet Archive capture served 2008-12-15): ""D. D. Scout Plane"'s effect can only activate once during the same End Phase, so if a combo of "Banisher of the Light" and "King Tiger Wanghu" is set up, "D. D. Scout Plane" will only be Special Summoned once." Konami TCG Card FAQ default_de page (Internet Archive capture served 2008-12-15): "If "D. D. Scout Plane" is removed from play and then returned to the Graveyard with "Miracle Dig" the same turn, its effect is reset and it remains in the Graveyard and is not Special Summoned." No difference between the era card and the modern card is established.

review.notes:
upstream_implementations is empty. Packet anomaly: errata_page.english_versions begins at index 1 (DR2-EN012, 2005-10-20) - there is no index 0 in the packet, so the card's original-printing English text is not available and a GOAT-era snapshot maps to the v1 wording by default. v1 and v2 are behaviourally identical, so this does not affect resolution, only displayed text. Chain therefore starts at v1; the text in force at the 2010-04-24 Edison snapshot is v2 (SDDE-EN011, 2008-04-02), with the erratum arriving 2012-09-29, well after. Trailing v3 -> v4 (SGX3-ENF07, 2023-03-30) only moves the once-per-turn clause to the end as 'This effect can only activate once per turn'; it is the pinned cdb text and is cosmetic. No entry for this card in edison-functional-errata.md (its sibling D.D. Survivor does appear there).

Round 037 (2026-09-29). Checked against period rulings: the differences the functional transition claims were searched for in the Konami-hosted UDE card FAQ (2008-12), the 2005 UDE card rulings page, Konami's errata lists, rulebooks and per-set ruling documents, and the archived UDE judge-list threads Yugipedia points to (the transition's rulings_check; docs/research/text-only-errata-audit.md, D.D. Scout Plane). A period ruling in force contradicts every difference the transition claimed: The era card has no once-per-turn limit, so a copy banished again during the same End Phase (for example by Bottomless Trap Hole) returns again; the modern card returns once per turn. Contradicted by Konami TCG Card FAQ default_de page (Internet Archive capture served 2008-12-15): ""D. D. Scout Plane"'s effect can only activate once during the same End Phase, so if a combo of "Banisher of the Light" and "King Tiger Wanghu" is set up, "D. D. Scout Plane" will only be Special Summoned once." Upper Deck Entertainment official Yu-Gi-Oh! Card Rulings page (Internet Archive replay): ""D. D. Scout Plane"'s effect can only activate once during the same End Phase, so if a combo of "Banisher of the Light" and "King Tiger Wanghu" is set up, "D. D. Scout Plane" will only be Special Summoned once." The modern card checks that it is currently banished and was banished this turn; the era trigger is claimed to have no still-banished check. Contradicted by Konami TCG Card FAQ default_de page (Internet Archive capture served 2008-12-15): "If "D. D. Scout Plane" is removed from play and then returned to the Graveyard with "Miracle Dig" the same turn, its effect is reset and it remains in the Graveyard and is not Special Summoned." Konami TCG Card FAQ default_de page (Internet Archive capture served 2008-12-15): "If "D. D. Scout Plane" is removed during an End Phase, it is Special Summoned with its effect during that same End Phase." The transition is cosmetic: no difference between the era card and the modern card is established. Verdicts: [c1] d1 contradicted at Edison, contradicted at Tengu; d2 contradicted at Edison, contradicted at Tengu. Superseded summary, kept verbatim: "Functional erratum: LCYW-EN216 adds a once-per-turn limit ('Once per turn, during the End Phase') and a still-banished check ('if this card is currently banished, and was banished this turn') that the DR2/SDDE texts do not carry. Without the limit the trigger can fire again in the same End Phase after the card has already come back and been banished a second time (for example by a Bottomless Trap Hole answering the first return); the errata'd card returns once per turn only." Superseded coverage, kept verbatim: kind: "known-gap"; gap_reason: "Project Ignis ships no historical implementation of this card; reproducing the era behaviour needs a custom script and a reserved passcode"; gap_sources: ["ignis-babelcdb"; "yugipedia-card-errata"]. Superseded gap statement, kept verbatim: "In GOAT and Edison, D.D. Scout Plane's End Phase return has no once-per-turn cap, so a copy banished again during that same End Phase should come back again; the shipped card allows only one return per turn."
